claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi produced by SLM can have a single-phase FCC microstructure.
As-built SLM CoCrFeMnNi components exhibit residual porosity, microcracks, and undissolved high-melting particles.
These fabrication defects cause dimensional distortion and compromised mechanical properties in SLM HEAs.
A HIP treatment near 1100 °C and 150 MPa for 2–4 hours is an optimized or suitable treatment for the targeted SLM HEAs.
Post-build HIP is applicable to SLM HEAs having predominantly single-phase FCC or BCC microstructures.
High pressure and temperature during HIP enhance atomic diffusion and thereby close internal pores.
HIP heals microcracks in HEAs.
HIP homogenizes the microstructure and eliminates undissolved high-melting particles.
HIP decreases residual stresses in additively manufactured HEAs.
Void closure and crack healing reduce local stress concentrations.
HIP densifies the microstructure of SLM HEAs.
HIP-induced homogenization minimizes dimensional distortion.
HIP increases both yield strength and ductility relative to the untreated as-built state.
HIP-treated SLM HEA parts will have lower geometric deviations than untreated SLM parts.
HIP will decrease porosity in the targeted SLM HEAs to below approximately 0.5%.
HIP will improve key mechanical properties, including yield strength and ductility, by approximately 20–30%.
The intervention should be effective primarily for additively manufactured HEAs with relatively homogeneous single-phase microstructures.
HIP effectiveness may be limited when it induces adverse phase transformations, multiphase structures, or excessive grain coarsening.
The quantitative porosity and mechanical-property improvements depend on HIP parameters and alloy composition.

The hypothesis is to be rejected if HIP-treated specimens fail to show statistically significant improvements in dimensional precision, porosity, and mechanical properties relative to identical as-built controls, including porosity remaining above approximately 0.5%.
